pool.text: Henry Morton Stanley first traversed the area after navigating the rapids and falls.
Stanley returned to establish the initial trading post in the region.
Lieutenant Arvid Wester brokered a treaty with the Arab Swahili slavers.
Deane and Dubois set fire to the station and sought refuge.
Administrator General Camille Janssen issued a decree establishing nine districts within the colony.
The sprawling population required the District Commissioner to create a daily food market.
Place de la Femme was completed as a dedication to Boyomaise women.
A decree of Governor General established the city of Stanleyville.
Antoine Gizenga installed the Free Republic of the Congo in Stanleyville.
Stanleyville was under siege of the Simbas.
Stanleyville was renamed Kisangani as part of authenticité policies.
Kisangani was the site of the Stanleyville mutinies resulting in widespread looting.
The communes were renamed to new designations like Mangobo and Tshopo.
The city was the site of the first open fighting between Ugandan and Rwandan forces.
Clashes between Rwandan and Ugandan forces led to thousands of deaths and destruction.
160 people were massacred in Kisangani during the Second Congo War.
The Studios Kabako relocated to Kisangani.
The constitution proposed the subdivision of the territory into 26 provinces.
The Organic Law establishing the boundaries of the provinces was adopted.
It is the country's fifth-most populous urban area with an estimated population.
